comparison: Perfect agreement on overall statistical associations (C18, C19, C30). Both evaluations find these results SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the paradoxical decreased MI risk requires explanation, while peer reviewers accept findings without raising this concern.

Perfect agreement on continuous age analysis within breast cancer patients (C10, C11, C57, C58, C68). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes dose-response relationship and clinical meaningfulness; peer reviewers treat this as the central, accepted conclusion of the study.

Perfect agreement on propensity score matching analysis showing age-dependent gradient (C12, C23-C28, C59). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed interpretation of age-stratified effects; peer reviewers acknowledge propensity-matched findings without questioning validity.

Divergent evaluations on effect modification by hypertension and diabetes (C29). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of explicit interaction statistics and p-values. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting subgroup findings without raising concerns about statistical evidence.

Agreement on sensitivity analyses (C60-C64). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency strengthens findings but specific supplementary results not detailed. Peer reviewers accept robustness checks as part of compelling statistical analyses.

Agreement on clinical implications (C69, C70). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriately cautious recommendations; editor explicitly endorses need for cardiovascular monitoring in breast cancer patients.

Strong agreement on methodological strengths (C8-C17, C20, C39-C41, C43, C47-C52, C54-C56). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes ethical approval claims (C65-C67) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers. Peer reviewers add C45-C46 (methodology) to their evaluation. Both affirm study design, data sources, and analytical approach.

Divergent evaluations on mechanistic explanations (C31-C38). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and based on literature rather than direct measurements, lacking treatment-specific data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting mechanistic interpretations as standard contextual information without challenge.

Agreement on background claims (C1-C7). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations to established literature. Peer reviewers group these with other contextual claims (C21, C22, C31-C38, C42, C44) and accept as standard framing without specific discussion.

Partial overlap on methodological claims. OpenEval R8 addresses sample size and methodological advantages (C42, C44-C46) rated as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C45-C46 as part of broader methodological evaluation. Both affirm appropriateness of analytical approaches.

Minimal overlap on study characteristics. OpenEval R8 emphasizes large sample size and multi-source data advantage (C42, C44) rated as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes these claims (C42, C44) within broader contextual acceptance without specific discussion.

Minimal overlap on ethical claims (C65-C67). OpenEval R1 includes ethical approval as part of methodological strengths rated as SUPPORTED. Peer R9 groups ethical claims (C53, C65-C67) as standard administrative elements implicitly accepted without question.
